slides.texte_overlay:
How to never run out of
things to say with a girl
Ask about her week, not her job. "What was the best part of your week?" It invites a story instead of a job title, and stories lead to more questions.
Talk about what's around you. The music, the place, the people walking by. The moment you're sharing is always an easy topic. Start with what you both see.
Share a small funny story about yourself. A cooking disaster, a wrong train, a silly mistake. Laughing at yourself makes the conversation relaxed.
Ask "how did you get into that?" about anything she loves. Climbing, painting, a band. People love telling the story of how their passions started.
Keep your life interesting. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and having new things in my head makes conversations flow naturally.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. New things in my head make conversations flow naturally.

slides.texte_overlay: Talk about plans and dreams. A trip she wants to take, something she's always wanted to learn. Future plans are light, fun and personal.
Don't be scared of a pause. A smile and a sip of your drink are enough. Comfortable silences are a good sign, not a problem to fix.
